title: I’m building a cell evolution game with ChatGPT/Codex and would love some honest playtest feedback
author: leonitusz
selftext:
Düzenle

Hey everyone! I’ve been building **MIKRO**, a browser game where you start as a tiny cell, find food, evolve, and divide to grow your lineage.

You can develop into a predator, rely on photosynthesis, or form a colony with specialized cells. When your cell dies, you can continue as a surviving relative. There’s also a family tree so you can follow what happens to your descendants.

I’m using ChatGPT/Codex for development and iterating on the mechanics based on feedback. It’s still an early prototype, and I’d really appreciate people trying it for a few minutes.

**Play here:** [https://mikro-yasam-hp.fatihsezer17.chatgpt.site](https://mikro-yasam-hp.fatihsezer17.chatgpt.site)

I’m particularly curious about:

Is the opening fun, or does progression feel too slow?Which mechanics are confusing or frustrating?nWhat would make you want to keep playing?

Performance is still a known issue for some players. I’ve made another optimization pass, but if you get low FPS, please mention your device and browser. You can enable the FPS counter in Settings.

Desktop controls: WASD/arrow keys or hold the mouse button to move. Touch controls are also available.

Honest criticism is welcome—even “I stopped after two minutes because…” would be useful.
